subject: Logic
title: The Trolley Problem
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Trolley Problem.

hook.text: A trolley is heading toward five people. You can switch it to a track with one person. Do you pull?

buildup.text: Utilitarians say pull: five lives saved is better than one. But you're actively choosing to harm someone.

discovery.text: The variant: push a large man off a bridge to stop the trolley. Same math, but most people refuse.

twist.text: The difference is personal involvement. We accept diverting harm but recoil from directly causing it.

climax.text: The trolley problem reveals that moral intuition and moral logic often point in different directions.

quiz.question: What does the trolley problem reveal about moral reasoning?
